title: Human Post Mortem Brain Processing
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bf4ajqse
materials: Cavex Life Cast Normal Alginate (Cavex Holland ALGINATE)
Fresh Human Brain (whole or single hemisphere)
Large plastic bin(s) for freezing tissue
Teflon coated freezing plates (small and large)
Vacuum Seal bags: 1 pint (Jarden Store FSFSBF0116-000)
Fume hood or Biological Safety Cabinet (BSC)
Methodology/Procedures: Removal of the brainstem and cerebellum
Methodology/Procedures: Slabbing and Freezing the Brainstem.

steps.title: Prepare alginate embedding solution
steps.instruction: Immediately before use, make alginate by mixing 270 g Cavex Alginate (≈½ pack) into 2000 mL Milli‑Q water in a Waring high‑speed blender, snap on the foam arrestor, blend on high for 30 s until no dry powder remains, then turn off the blender and remove the arrestor.

steps.title: Set up cerebrum embedding chambers
steps.instruction: Line each cerebrum chamber with a large clear plastic bag and insert the plastic plates; secure plates with bulldog clips, mark the bag with D‑ventral, V‑ventral, A‑anterior, P‑posterior, then pour alginate to ~2/3 of chamber height.

steps.title: Create hemispheric alginate cavities
steps.instruction: Place the sagittal brain mold (left or right hemisphere) into the alginate‑filled chamber, immerse ~½ of the mold so its long (anterior‑posterior) axis stays parallel to the chamber sides, hold until alginate sets enough to prevent sinking, then transfer the chamber to 4 °C until embedding.

steps.title: Prepare cerebellum embedding chamber
steps.instruction: Line a small‑bag chamber with a clear plastic bag, insert plastic plates and secure with bulldog clips; pour ≈2 inches of alginate into the mold, place at 4 °C to harden, then scoop out a cavity roughly the size of the cerebellum and notch a small amount of alginate from each corner to create a lock‑and‑key for the top layer.

steps.title: Prepare dry‑ice/isopentane freezing bath
steps.instruction: In an ice bucket, add enough isopentane to submerge ~⅓ of the tissue height and add dry‑ice pellets to reach a slurry temperature of –60 °C to –70 °C (monitor with a Fluke meter); keep the isopentane level ~⅓ from the tissue top, never fully submerge tissue, and add fresh isopentane for each hemisphere or cerebellum.

steps.title: Receive brain and document
steps.instruction: Remove the brain from its shipment container, weigh it on a balance, record the weight, and photograph ventral, dorsal, lateral and posterior views with visible labels.

steps.title: Mark cerebellum inferior surface
steps.instruction: Using a wooden‑handled swab, apply black India ink to the inferior surface of the cerebellum; optionally add a second line of a different color (green, blue, white, or yellow) on the anatomical left side from midline to the left pole, and place a black dot opposite the lines.

steps.title: Separate cerebellum and brainstem
steps.instruction: Make a transverse cut below the inferior and superior colliculi (avoiding the thalamus) to remove the cerebellum and brainstem as a single block; photograph the separated pieces and place both on wet ice until further processing.

steps.title: Hemisection of cerebrum
steps.instruction: Place the cerebrum ventral side down, pull temporal lobes away from the midline, separate hemispheres to expose the corpus callosum, bisect the brain with a sharp Mopec knife through the corpus callosum, mammillary bodies and optic chiasm, photograph medial and lateral surfaces of each hemisphere, record all measurements per the TPS report, and keep hemispheres on wet ice.

steps.title: Embed each cerebral hemisphere
steps.instruction: For each hemisphere, place the medial surface up in its pre‑made alginate mold (enlarge cavity if needed), insert a long cotton‑swab marker adjacent to the frontal and occipital poles (different colors for anterior‑posterior), optionally cut 2 cm³ alginate from each corner of the base, indicate dorsal, ventral, anterior and posterior on the mold or bag, pour alginate to fill crevices while leaving the medial face exposed, let harden at 4 °C, then mark the alginate surface with D‑V‑A‑P orientation.

steps.title: Prepare brainstem slab labels and ice
steps.instruction: Label five brainstem slabs as BS.91 (midbrain), BS.92 (rostral pons), BS.93 (caudal pons), BS.94 (rostral medulla), BS.95 (caudal medulla); set up a bucket of wet ice covered with a layer of Saran wrap or absorbent pad, and use an India‑ink pen to place orientation marks on the ventral surface at the midbrain/pons junction, middle of pons, and middle of medulla.

steps.title: Section brainstem into slabs
steps.instruction: Place the brainstem on a cutting board, align the steel blocking blade with the orientation marks and make a transverse cut; mark the dorsal/rostral surface of BS.91, then cut the pons into rostral (BS.92) and caudal (BS.93) blocks, marking each dorsal/rostral surface with a black ink dot; finally separate the medulla into rostral (BS.94) and caudal (BS.95) blocks, keep all five slabs on the chilled absorbent pad.

steps.title: Freeze brainstem slabs
steps.instruction: Spray two 4 × 4 in. Teflon plates with Blue Works Dry Lube; place each slab (starting with BS.91, black‑dot side up) on the lower plate, sandwich with the upper plate, and submerge the assembly in the –60 °C to –70 °C isopentane/dry‑ice slurry until solid (2–4 min, tap with metal forceps to confirm); remove plates, place slab on dry ice, vacuum‑seal in a bag with label visible, and store at –80 °C. Repeat for BS.92‑95.

steps.title: Embed and slice cerebellum
steps.instruction: Place the cerebellum smooth (superior) side down in its alginate block so the anterior (cut from brainstem) faces up; insert a wooden‑handled swab marked with yellow/orange ink at the left‑right lateral aspects, deflect alginate with a spatula to fully encase the tissue, let harden at 4 °C, then mark the alginate surface with D‑V‑A‑P orientation; remove the block, position the left‑lateral marker toward the slicer guide, and cut sagittally left‑to‑right at 1.5 cm intervals. After each cut, coat a Teflon plate with Blue Works, sandwich the cut slab between plates, insert a plastic plate between cut and uncut portions, lower the plate to expose the slab, and ink the superior right face. Remove all alginate, photograph each slab with its label, coat the posterior surface with a second Blue Works plate (except for the first and last slabs), flip the slab 180° so the posterior side contacts the plate, and proceed to freezing.

steps.title: Freeze cerebellum slabs
steps.instruction: Add dry ice to the isopentane slurry to keep it at –60 °C to –70 °C, place each slab (with its two lubricated plates) into the slurry until fully frozen (tap to confirm), immediately transfer the slab with chilled metal forceps into a vacuum‑seal bag (left side facing the smooth bag side, label visible), seal, place on dry ice, and store in a –80 °C freezer. Repeat for all cerebellar slabs.

steps.title: Slice cerebral hemispheres
steps.instruction: After the top alginate layer has set, remove each hemisphere block, place it on the slabbing apparatus with the frontal‑pole marker forward, make an initial cut with a Mopec knife just in front of the frontal marker to remove excess alginate, then cut the embedded hemisphere into 1 cm anterior‑to‑posterior slabs (number left‑hemisphere slabs 1‑20, right‑hemisphere slabs 40‑59). Every 3‑4 slabs, capture a top‑down image of the medial surface and knife angle. After each cut, spray a Teflon plate with Blue Works, sandwich the cut slab between the plate and a second plate, insert a plastic plate to create a sandwich, lower the plate to reveal the slab, remove remaining alginate, reposition tissue symmetrically, replace any mis‑aligned gyri, remove meninges from the posterior surface, ink the white‑matter region on the posterior/medial/dorsal surface with ~0.5 µL India ink, label and photograph the slab, then sandwich with a second lubricated plate, flip 180° so the posterior surface contacts the plate, and freeze as described for cerebellum slabs (isopentane slurry, tap, vacuum‑seal, store at –80 °C).

steps.title: Final cleanup and waste disposal
steps.instruction: Soak all instruments in 10 % bleach for ≥30 min, rinse and dry; dispose of excess alginate in biohazard waste; discard Mopec knives in biohazard sharps containers; when returning used isopentane, pour it back into its container without the lid, let it equilibrate to room temperature in the hood, then replace the lid; verify that all frozen slabs are in the –80 °C freezer, perform a physical inventory against the slabbing manifest, record any missing items on the TPS report, and ensure any blood, CSF, or other tissue specimens are properly stored.
